1.title: Welcome to Klaro
1.description: Klaro is a free service. Klaro helps you understand social support better.

2.title: This is about social benefits
2.description: Klaro currently checks the following social benefits: basic income support, basic income in old age, housing benefit and the child supplement. You can see which support could fit you.

3.title: Answer a few short questions
3.description: With a few questions, Klaro checks your situation. That gives you an initial orientation.

4.title: Start the check now
4.description: The check only takes a few minutes. You can start right away and don't need an account yet.

householdComposition.title: Who lives in your household?
householdComposition.tip: How many people live together changes the calculation. Children count too.

options.COUPLE_NO_CHILDREN: We are a couple, without children in the household.
options.COUPLE_WITH_CHILDREN: We are a couple, with children in the household.

children.title: When were your children born?
children.tip: Your children's ages matter because separate amounts apply to children. Some benefits only exist for children under 18 or under 25.

dateOfBirth.title: When were you born?
dateOfBirth.tip: Your age helps decide which benefits may apply to you. Different rules apply once you reach the standard retirement age.

livesInGermany.title: Do you live in Germany?
livesInGermany.tip: The benefits Klaro checks are only available if you live in Germany permanently.

isEmployed.title: Are you currently working?
isEmployed.tip: If you live with a partner, their work counts too.

monthlyGrossIncome.title: What is the monthly gross income?
monthlyGrossIncome.tip: Gross means the amount before taxes and contributions. You can find it on your payslip. If you live with a partner, add both together.

workCapacity.title: Can you work at least three hours a day?
workCapacity.tip: Three hours is a limit set by law. It decides which office is responsible for you. We also ask if you work: some people work in a sheltered workshop, for example, and still count as having reduced earning capacity.

options.FULL: Yes, at least three hours a day.
options.TEMPORARILY_REDUCED: Not at the moment, but maybe again later.

monthlyNetHouseholdIncome.title: How much money does your household have per month in total?
monthlyNetHouseholdIncome.tip: Add up everything that comes in each month: wages after deductions, pension, child benefit, maintenance, other benefits. An approximate amount is enough.

monthlyWarmRent.title: How much is your monthly rent including utilities?
monthlyWarmRent.tip: This means rent plus service charges plus heating costs. The amount is in your tenancy agreement or on your bank statement.

assetsBand.title: How much money have you saved?
assetsBand.tip: This means everything you have put aside: account, savings book, cash, securities. You may keep part of it — how much depends on your age. A rough estimate is enough.

receivesBenefits.title: Do you already receive a social benefit?
receivesBenefits.tip: For example basic income support, basic income in old age or subsistence assistance. Some benefits cannot be received at the same time.

citizenship.title: What is your citizenship?
citizenship.tip: Different laws apply depending on citizenship and residence status.

options.NON_EU: From a country outside the EU.

hasSecureResidenceStatus.title: Do you have a secure residence permit?
hasSecureResidenceStatus.tip: Secure means, for example: settlement permit, permanent residence permit or recognition as a refugee. If you are still in the asylum procedure, there is a separate system — Klaro will point this out at the end.

options.NO: No, or I am not sure.

eligible.title: Your initial assessment
eligible.cta: Create account and fill in application

not_eligible.title: You are not entitled to these benefits.
not_eligible.description: The benefits Klaro checks are only available if you live in Germany permanently.

benefits.GRUNDSICHERUNG_ALTER: Basic income in old age and for reduced earning capacity

status.POSSIBLE: You could be entitled – have it checked

reasons.income_covers_needs: Your income covers your needs including rent.
reasons.assets_too_high: Your savings are above the amount you may keep.
reasons.assets_near_limit: Your savings are around the amount you may keep.
reasons.income_below_needs: Your income does not cover your needs including rent.
reasons.retirement_age_reached: You have reached the standard retirement age.
reasons.permanently_unable_to_work: You can permanently work less than three hours a day.
reasons.temporarily_unable_to_work: Whether you need to be able to work for this depends on how long you cannot work.
reasons.not_retired_nor_unable_to_work: You have not reached the standard retirement age and are able to work.
reasons.income_too_low_for_wohngeld: Your income is too low for housing benefit. Another benefit fits better.
reasons.high_rent_share: Your rent is high compared to your income.
reasons.low_rent_share: Your rent is not high compared to your income.
reasons.no_children: No children under 25 live in your household.
reasons.gross_below_minimum: Your gross income is below the minimum income for the child supplement.
reasons.gross_above_minimum: Your gross income reaches the minimum income for the child supplement.
reasons.already_receives_benefits: You already receive a social benefit. Some benefits cannot be received at the same time.
reasons.residence_status_unclear: Whether you are entitled depends on your residence status.

outcome.residence_hint: If you are in the asylum procedure or have a toleration permit (Duldung), you receive benefits under the Asylum Seekers' Benefits Act. Contact the State Office for Refugee Affairs or the social welfare office.
outcome.disclaimer: This is a non-binding, automatic initial assessment and not legal advice. The responsible office decides whether you are entitled.
